entities.summary: Nino Burjanadze is a Georgian politician and lawyer who served as Chairperson of the Parliament of Georgia from November 2001 to June 2008. As the first woman, she served as the acting head of state of Georgia twice; the first time from 23 November 2003 to 25 January 2004 in the wake of Eduard Shevardnadze's resignation during the Rose Revolution, and again from 25 November 2007 to 20 January 2008, after Mikheil Saakashvili stepped down to run in the early presidential election. She withdrew into opposition to Saakashvili as the leader of the Democratic Movement – United Georgia party in 2008.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Nino Burjanadze's two terms as acting head of state had significant regional impact in Georgia, shaping its political trajectory after the Rose Revolution and influencing the country's leadership transition. Her tenure also marked a milestone for women in politics.
